text:
Kirill Kaprizov came to San Jose with headlines saying he was chasing a franchise record, and he left with a goal, three assists and a point streak that Heather Rule of NHL.com put at 15 games. Five of those 15 have been three-point nights or better. Minnesota won 5-2, and he had a hand in four of them.

It was not as tidy as the score. Kaprizov opened it on a first-period power play, then the Sharks answered twice: Tyler Toffoli banked in a backhand on a chance we rated at 1%, and Alexander Wennberg ended a scoring slump at 17:29 for a 2-1 San Jose lead. Brock Faber, an unlikely source on a 2% look, tied it with 41.6 seconds left in the period, his second goal of the season. Thirteen seconds into the second, Joel Eriksson Ek went bar down, and the Wild never trailed again. That goal moved their win chance from 48% to 66%, the biggest swing of the night.

The expected goals (3.51 to 1.71) flatter Minnesota. At even strength the Sharks had the better chances, 1.41 to 0.84, and the Wild's total leaned on a strong power play and two late goals, Blake Coleman at 18:24 and Eriksson Ek's second at 19:06. Deserved to win, the share of replays of every shot a team wins, landed at 59% for Minnesota: a real edge, not a rout. Filip Gustavsson's best stop came on Wennberg in the third with the score still 3-2.

Matt Boldy added three assists and Eriksson Ek finished with three points, and the Wild did it all while still without Quinn Hughes, on injured reserve since the hit in Calgary last week. That is two wins over San Jose this month, after a 4-1 result on Nov. 6.

For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini set up both goals, and Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest counted 18 points in nine career games against Minnesota. Michael Misa stretched his point streak to four. Yaroslav Askarov allowed three goals on 28 shots, about 0.9 more than they deserved.
headline: Kaprizov runs the streak to 15 as Wild handle Sharks
